🤥 Trump weighs renewed war on Iran as Israel lobbies for days-long bombing campaign
Even after Donald Trump signaled last week that a major new round of strikes on Iran was "quite unlikely," discussions about a joint attack with Israel are expected to intensify after his return from Asia, reports Axios.
Trump is reportedly weighing a military campaign targeting suspected nuclear sites such as Pickaxe Mountain, along with bridges, power infrastructure, and Iranian military and civilian leadership.
The US president is under competing pressures, notes the publication:
👉 Benjamin Netanyahu, facing domestic political challenges, is pushing hard for rapid resumption of hostilities
👉 Gulf leaders, concerned about potential Iranian retaliation against their energy facilities, are urging continued economic pressure instead of open conflict
👉 some senior administration figures favor military action; the WH has publicly emphasized the impact of sanctions, yet insisted all options remain available 
Trump has reportedly sought detailed assessments from the Pentagon and intel community on how Iran might respond to various strike scenarios, specifically asking whether any of them could avoid catastrophic retaliation against Gulf oil and gas infrastructure.
Israel’s Mossad chief Roman Gofman is described as having recently visited the US for talks with CIA leadership, conveying concerns about allegedly expanded Iranian work on chemical and biological weapons.
US and Israeli officials are said to disagree on how imminent any actual capability is.
A NTY report also claims that Trump is considering a new wave of military strikes on Iran, with Israel pressing the US to launch a four-to-seven-day bombing campaign.
He is reportedly sensitive to accusations that the US has lost the Iran war and sees renewed military action as one way to demonstrate strength.

🔍 Four theories behind US outages – from an AI giants’ plot to a Netanyahu false flag
US outages remain unexplained, with the Trump administration and the US intelligence community struggling to calm Americans.
💬 US President Donald Trump said, “It’s life, it’s life,” effectively downplaying the troubling trend. US Secretary of State Marco Rubio acknowledged growing fears among Americans but sought to reassure the public, saying there was "zero evidence" the incidents were connected or that a cyberattack was underway.
👉 Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton claimed the disruptions were caused by maintenance and technical changes, but failed to dispel concerns over the strange coincidence of so many incidents occurring within just one week.
Observers say the incidents bear all the hallmarks of a systemic attack targeting vital nodes of US digital infrastructure and communications.
1️⃣Some netizens point to earlier warnings by Anthropic and other tech giants that artificial intelligence could independently escape a test sandbox and wreak havoc. Some unexplained hacking operations of this kind have already taken place.
2️⃣ Others speculate that supposedly rogue AI agents causing chaos could actually be directed by tech billionaires themselves. The idea is that they create the problem so they can sell the solution, consolidate control over the industry and delay the looming AI bubble burst.
3️⃣ Some media personalities have blamed Iran and possibly Russia, suggesting they could have launched a cyberattack against the US. They predict that after disruptions to America's water systems, flights and banks, the power grid could be the next target.
4️⃣ Another theory points to Israel. Israeli intelligence agencies are known for their hacking operations, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu recently identified AI as a field in which Israel aims to become a global leader. Tel Aviv also has a potential motive: unhappy that the US has not resumed the war against Iran, Israel could be lashing out and creating chaos to send a message, particularly as reports of an alleged Iranian dirty bomb appear to be gaining little traction.
The flurry of speculation makes one thing clear: few believe this is merely a coincidence or simply a combination of incompetence and America's crumbling, aging infrastructure.
